subject: Subprocessor access matrix / onboarding playbook request
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@carewellhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Carewell Procurement <procurement@carewellhealth.com>, SecurityOps <security@carewellhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor access & onboarding questions

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the demo last week. As we start contracting conversations I need two things to move this internally: a completed subprocessor access matrix (who at Redwood can access PII, under what role boundary, and whether KMS keys are customer-managed) and a simple diagram/dataflow showing where PII touches Redwood services (ingest, KV cache, logs, telemetry). Procurement asked for the matrix and Security wants the flow to slot into our SSQ.

A few specific asks up-front:
- Can you confirm whether any Redwood subprocessors process raw PII outside the US? If so, which ones and for what purpose.
- Do you offer a private/VPC deployment option where data and keys remain in our account?
- What attestations do you provide for KMS operations (exportability, split keys, HSM-backed)?

Can you send the access matrix template and a short plan for producing these artifacts? We have an internal deadline next Friday for the procurement packet.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a 30m call if useful.

Best,
Emma Li
Head of Vendor Risk
Carewell Health

Attachments: carewell_ssq_v1.pdf (initial SSQ we've started)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@carewellhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor access & onboarding questions

Hi Emma —

Thanks — and great to engage. I’ve attached a lightweight subprocessor access matrix template and a short onboarding playbook that maps the artifacts we'll produce. High level answers here:
- Redwood runs most telemetry & host-level ops with a small set of subprocessors; we produce a residency map per-customer during onboarding. I’ll flag any subprocessors that process raw PII outside the US in the completed matrix.
- Yes: our Private deployment supports VPC mode with customer-controlled KMS (bring-your-own-key or external HSM integration).
- For KMS we provide a key custody statement and can provide HSM-backed attestations or a KMS proxy architecture where customer keys remain in their cloud project.

I’ve pulled Kimberly in to provide the attestation sketch and Marissa to own the artifact delivery schedule. I’m copying procurement in case you want to align on timeline/billing.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Gxq-example-link-subprocessor-matrix
Attachments: subprocessor_access_matrix_template.xlsx; canary_onboarding_plan.pdf

Next step: Kimberly/Marissa — can you confirm the specific artifacts (evidence types) we should include for Carewell’s packet and whether a short architecture diagram (PNG/PDF) will suffice for the SSQ?

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@carewellhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor access & onboarding questions

Jordan / Marissa —

Thanks Emma — tagging a few technical clarifications so we can produce the right artifacts:
1) KMS attestation: we can provide an HSM-backed key custody diagram and a statement on exportability. For BYOK in our Private deployment, keys stay in customer cloud KMS; for hosted deployments we offer a KMS proxy option that prevents key export.
2) Access matrix fields we need: subprocessor name, purpose, region(s) of processing, roles with access (SRE, platform-ops, privacy-ops), type of data accessed (ingest/raw, tokens/KV, telemetry), and evidence (audit log snippet, runbook excerpt).
3) Logs and telemetry: by default we collect anonymized inference telemetry; PII-containing payloads are redacted in transit and TTLed. If customer needs redaction guarantees at ingest, we provide an L7 proxy pattern as an add-on.

I’ve attached a short KMS attestation overview that we can hand to procurement/security as a first draft.

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kms_attestation_overview.pdf
From: Emma Li <emma.li@carewellhealth.com>

Cc: Carewell Procurement <procurement@carewellhealth.com>, SecurityOps <security@carewellhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 10:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor access & onboarding questions

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from Security/Procurement:
- Cross-border transfers: Carewell requires confirmation that no raw patient identifiers are sent to subprocessors outside the US without a documented legal basis. If Redwood has a specific subprocessors list that might process tokenized or raw content outside the US, please flag those rows in the matrix.
- Evidence: Security will accept audit log snippets (redacted) + runbook excerpt + KMS statement. If you can mark which evidence is "redacted-audit" vs "full-audit" in the matrix that will help us triage.
- Timing: Procurement needs the packet (matrix + diagram + KMS attestation) by EOD Friday to make the vendor packet for their weekly committee.

We’re open to a 30m call tomorrow to walk through the matrix fields. Are you available 10–10:30am PT?

Emma

Emma / team —

Good call today — summary and next steps below (timeline targeted to your Friday procurement deadline):

Summary of artifacts we will deliver by EOD Friday (5/7):
- Completed subprocessor access matrix (CSV/XLSX) with region flags and evidence column (we’ll mark rows that reference non-US processing and evidence type: redacted-audit / runbook / KMS-statement).
- One-page dataflow diagram (PDF) showing ingress, KV cache, telemetry, and retention boundaries.
- KMS attestation bundle (PDF) describing BYOK options, HSM-backed custody, and proxy architecture.
- DPA amendment draft (Word) that adds the subprocessor inventory exhibit; we’ll provide a DocuSign link for signature if you’re ready.

Notes / answers to your questions:
- Cross-border: At present, a small set of telemetry subprocessors operate in EU/APAC for telemetry ingestion and availability; they do not store raw patient identifiers and are marked in the matrix. If Carewell requires absolute residency we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) with BYOK; we’ll include a short migration plan in the playbook.
- Evidence levels: we will tag each matrix row with evidence type. For security convenience we will include a sample redacted-audit snippet inline in the bundle. Full audit extracts can be produced under an NDA/escrow process.
- Onboarding cadence: Marissa will own the artifact delivery and a week-one runbook. Priyom will coordinate customer-specific model routing and geofencing steps for Private deployments.

Action items:
- Marissa: attach finalized matrix and runbook excerpt here by EOD Fri.
- Kimberly: finalize the KMS attestation PDF (attached) and confirm whether additional HSM supplier proofs are required.
- Emma: confirm if DocuSign flow is OK for the DPA amendment and whether Procurement wants redlines returned or a markup call.
